a11yToolbarTooltip.message: Check the content for accessibility issues

a11yImageAltWhy.message: Screen readers need an alt attribute to describe an image or identify it as decorative.

a11yImageAltFilenameMessage.message: Image alternative text should describe the image, not repeat its filename.

a11yImageAltFilenameWhy.message: A filename rarely gives screen reader users useful information about an image.

a11yImageAltLengthMessage.message: Image alternative text should be 125 characters or fewer.

a11yImageAltLengthWhy.message: Short descriptions are easier to understand and navigate with assistive technology.

a11yHeadingSequenceMessage.message: Heading levels should not skip levels.

a11yHeadingSequenceWhy.message: A logical heading outline helps people navigate content with assistive technology.

a11yTableHeaderWhy.message: Header cells give screen readers the context needed to understand table data.

a11yTableCaptionWhy.message: A caption identifies a table's purpose before a screen reader enters its cells.

a11yTableHeaderScopeMessage.message: Table header cells should declare their scope.

a11yTableHeaderScopeWhy.message: The scope attribute lets assistive technology associate headers with data cells.

a11yAdjacentLinksMessage.message: Adjacent links with the same destination should be combined.

a11yAdjacentLinksWhy.message: Repeated links create unnecessary stops for keyboard and screen reader users.

a11yHeadingStartMessage.message: The first heading should be an h2.

a11yHeadingStartWhy.message: The editor's document title is supplied outside the editable content.

a11yListStructureMessage.message: List items must be contained by an ordered or unordered list.

a11yListStructureWhy.message: Assistive technology relies on list structure to announce item counts and position.
